title.en: Disclose vertical exaggeration wherever slope is read

summary: State the vertical scale factor whenever it differs from the horizontal one, because slopes and volumes become unreadable without it.
objective: Keep an expressive terrain from being read as a measurement of steepness.
applies_when: Terrain, bathymetry or a profile is stretched vertically for legibility.
The scene shows slope, relief or a cross-section.
A viewer might compare steepness between features or scenes.
example_prompts: Exaggerate the relief but tell me by how much.
Show a terrain profile with an honest vertical scale.
negative_signals: Terrain rendered at true scale, where no disclosure is needed beyond the units.
Invented landscapes that make no measurement claim.
not_for: Terrain rendered at true scale, where no disclosure is needed beyond the units.
Invented landscapes that make no measurement claim.

principles: Vertical exaggeration is often necessary. At regional scale, true-scale relief is nearly invisible, so a scene that refuses to exaggerate may communicate nothing.

It is also a transformation of the reading. Scaling the vertical axis by a factor multiplies the tangent of every slope by the same factor, so an exaggerated hillside looks like a cliff and a gentle trench looks like a canyon.
The factor is cheap to disclose and impossible to infer. Without it, a viewer cannot compare steepness between two views, let alone against reality.
Volumes and cut-and-fill quantities are affected as well, so any quantitative readout must be computed at true scale even when the display is exaggerated.
implementation: Keep the true-scale elevation in the model and apply exaggeration as a display transform with an explicit factor.
Display the factor persistently, and include it in any exported image or clip.
Compute slopes, volumes and profiles from the true-scale data regardless of the display factor.
Offer a control to return to true scale so the viewer can calibrate what they are seeing.
Include a vertical scale bar or a reference object of known height in profile views.
observable_checks: Switch to true scale and confirm the geometry flattens by exactly the stated factor.
Compare a computed slope value against the visual impression at the current exaggeration.
Confirm exported images carry the factor.
Check that reported volumes do not change when the display factor changes.

creative_affordances: Dramatic relief is a legitimate and often necessary artistic choice; only the disclosure is required.
Animating between true and exaggerated scale is an effective way to convey both.
known_limits: Authored presentation guidance based on the elementary geometry of scaling one axis; no external source is cited and no cartographic standard is asserted.
It does not recommend a particular exaggeration factor for any application.
